post.0:
I finished third with 49 after leading into round III at 26. Last Call plus Pocket Watch carried me through rounds I and II, but in round III I cashed everything into followers right away and went quiet for ten rival turns with zero resources and two cheap members on the table. Ben poached Line Cutters and then Shake Down took Closer because I held only 2 and couldn't pay 5, and that same stretch let Ben chain Right Away and Crunch Time into a Hot Streak for 9, which I had flagged and could have bought myself. The deciding moment was that 10-buy on my first round III turn: safe against steals, but it left me nothing to defend my members with. Cal won quietly on white conversions, a late Raiders and a big 10-buy, without ever being the obvious leader.

FEEL: Fence | 2 | 2 | yes | the one I'd least want: Cal got a handful of magenta from it and the steals mostly got blocked late.
FEEL: Line Cutters | 4 | 5 | unsure | 3 followers for 2 is underpriced and going first is real, but it's a Poach and Shake Down magnet.
FEEL: Closer | 4 | 4 | yes | basically free in a Last Call round, and Shake Down took it the next round.
FEEL: Hot Streak | 5 | 4 | yes | I spotted it for my four-turn run, passed for safety, and Ben used it for 9; my biggest regret.
FEEL: Gossip | 3 | 2 | yes | weighed it with all the skips, but 6 for 1 follower needs too many skips to pay.
FEEL: Clockmakers | 2 | 2 | yes | 5 for 2 followers and a turn order quirk, never close to buying a 5-follower buy instead.
FEEL: HR | 3 | 2 | unsure | considered it with Splurge for about 9 followers; 10 any for 4 is poor and the game-end bonus is hard to hit.
META: Contests and the 1:1 follower buy dominate the math, and purple's skip engine with Pocket Watch is strong and fun. Theft is the big swing: Help Yourself, Poach and Shake Down punish whoever holds a lead or a cheap member, and the only answers are Lie Low and Bodyguards, so a player who converts to stay safe just becomes a member-steal target instead. Late white spaces (Farewell, Cash In) were dead for anyone but the white leader. First thing I'd change: make Poach and Shake Down cost the thief something or cap them, since losing a member for nothing late in round III felt worse than any resource steal.
post.1:
I lost to Cal by 12, and I gave away the Purple 10 myself. On my last turn I spent 2 purple on a 5-follower buy because I'd counted Ava's ceiling at 7, and forgot that her two Last Call skips each fed Pocket Watch, so she finished 9 to my 8. Holding those 2 purple flips that contest, a 20-point swing, and puts me level with Cal before his Raiders took 4 off me. I'd assumed Bodyguards covered stolen followers and it doesn't. The round III run itself was the fun part: Crowd In, Right Away into Crunch Time for four in a row, Shake Down taking Ava's Closer because her pile was empty, Hot Streak for +9, and Heiresses for +13 white off 13 members. Cal won by sitting behind Lie Low every round with Fence and turning a huge pile into a 10-buy plus Exchange at the end, and nobody could ever touch his pile.

META: The contests drive everything, and the steals and skips around them give real last-turn swings, which is the best part of the game. What isn't working is protection: Lie Low gives one player a full round of immunity every round for one placement, and Last Call plus Pocket Watch turns one purple space into three payouts and the last word in the round. I'd change Lie Low first, maybe so it only blocks resource steals or only lasts until your next turn, and I'd make Bodyguards say plainly that follower steals like Raiders still go through.
post.2:
I won 66 to Ben's 54 and Ava's 49, and it came down to my last two placements in round III. Ben had just hit 48 off Crunch Time, Hot Streak and a 13-white Heiresses, and I was at 31. Stash took away Ava's only magenta, Raiders off the Stash took 4 from Ben, and Exchange plus a 10-buy cashed out everything but the 2 magenta I needed. I also left Ava's purple alone on purpose so her Hold Up could beat Ben's 8 for the +10, and that was the real 20-point swing. Lie Low every round was the quiet backbone: with Ava's Last Call stacking her placements at the end, being safe from steals let me sit on magenta and white leads without overbuying them.

META: The contests carry the game: magenta and white leads at +10 were worth more than any member, and choosing which color to hold and which to cash out was the best decision space we had. Last Call plus Pocket Watch, and Heiresses on a wide cult, are the two lines that look too strong, and Splurge and Cash In are nearly dead. In round III no member beats buying followers 1:1 unless a recruit bonus props it up, so the shop goes quiet just when the most is at stake. First change: tone down Last Call's block of end-of-round placements, maybe by capping the followers it gives or letting a rival act after it.
